title: ARQ, NAK and error correction
idea: ARQ answers every packet: ACK if it arrived clean, NAK to ask for it again, and too many failed tries drops the link. FEC sends redundant data so the receiver repairs errors itself.

rows: Redundant information sent with the data
Retries, timeouts, long pauses, failed connections: all of these

compare.how: Receiver replies ACK or NAK; bad packets are sent again.
No replies; extra redundant data lets the receiver fix errors.
Only detects an error in one character; it can't fix it.

traps.why: That's ACK. NAK means send it again.
Nothing overflows: after too many tries, ARQ simply drops the connection.

traps.wrong: By using a parity bit with each character
traps.why: A parity bit can only flag an error. FEC sends redundant data to fix it.
Routing goes up front, in the header.
A NAK asks for a resend; nothing lets a third station into a PACTOR link.
